docs.text:
I'm a technical writer and documentation engineer with a background in computer science. I specialize in developer-facing documentation: REST API references, architecture guides, and docs-as-code workflows that help engineers build, integrate, and troubleshoot systems.

Currently seeking: technical writer and documentation engineer roles. Open to remote work.

I built this portfolio with MkDocs Material and Markdown. I manage it in Git and deploy it with GitHub Pages.

docs.title: InSight clinical decision support documentation
docs.text:
Developer onboarding, a clinical operator guide, and an API reference for an AI-driven cataract screening service.

  • The problem: Clinical AI tools often run as opaque systems with isolated scripts. They lack reproducible local setups and clear interface contracts for integration engineers.
  • What I built:
    • A developer quickstart that covers environment isolation and local service startup.
    • An architecture overview that explains the pre-validation gate and Grad-CAM heatmaps.
    • An endpoint reference for POST /predict/ with multipart request examples in cURL and Python, binary image handling, and documented 422 and 500 error responses.
    • A clinical operator guide that walks nurses through screening, Grad-CAM interpretation, and referral report export.
  • My process: I analyzed the PyTorch inference engine and the FastAPI backend. I verified request and response cycles with cURL and Postman. I wrote separate paths for clinical and engineering audiences.
  • Skills shown: API reference design, architecture documentation, error state documentation, and Markdown.

docs.title: How I approach documentation
docs.text:
• Engineering empathy: Documentation should answer practical questions quickly. What is this service? How do I authenticate? What does a valid request look like? Why did my request fail?

  • Cross-functional verification: I interview subject matter experts (SMEs), compare requirements against QA test cases, and run commands locally to verify behavior before publishing.

docs.title: Case study: documenting the InSight clinical decision-support system
docs.text: How I organized documentation for two different audiences of one computer-vision cataract triage tool.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Project InSight cataract screening application Role Sole technical writer and documentation engineer Deliverables System overview, clinical operator guide, developer and API guide, OpenAPI specification Tools and standards MkDocs Material, Markdown, OpenAPI, Google Developer Documentation Style Guide, Git, GitHub Actions Audiences Frontline healthcare workers (operators) and software engineers (maintainers)

docs.title: 1. The problem
docs.text:
InSight is a machine learning tool that screens eye (fundus) photographs for signs of cataracts in low-resource clinics. The PyTorch model and FastAPI backend worked, but there was no documentation:

  • Operators had no instructions for capturing and uploading images, or for reading confidence scores and Grad-CAM heatmaps.
  • Engineers had no API specification, dependency map, or local setup guide.

The challenge was to document one product for two audiences with opposite needs, without confusing either.

docs.title: 2. The audiences
docs.text: Clinical operator Backend engineer Who Nurse, triage assistant, community health worker Full-stack developer, DevOps engineer, API consumer Goal Upload images, interpret risk tiers, export PDF referral reports Deploy the containers, integrate the REST API, debug inference issues Technical comfort Low High (terminal, Python, REST, JSON) What they need Visual, step-by-step tasks with screenshots OpenAPI contracts, cURL examples, status code tables, architecture

docs.title: 3. Information architecture
docs.text:
I split the content into three documents instead of one long page:

InSight documentation
├── System overview (insight.md)
│   └── Capabilities, clinical safety limits, architecture
├── Clinical operator guide (user-guide.md)
│   └── Image checks, step-by-step workflow, interpreting results
└── Developer and API guide (developer-guide.md)
    └── Setup, endpoints, error contracts, schemas

Two decisions shaped the structure:

  • Visible medical disclaimers. Warning callouts state that InSight is a decision-support aid, not a diagnostic authority.
  • Separation of concerns. Model details such as ResNet-18 weights and learning rates stay in the developer guide, so operators never meet them.

docs.title: 4. Editorial and technical approach
docs.text:
Style. I followed the Google Developer Documentation Style Guide:

  • Imperative, active verbs for steps ("Upload the fundus photograph," not "The photograph should be uploaded").
  • Sentence-case headings.
  • Captions and callouts on every screenshot, for screen-reader accessibility.

Docs-as-code.

  • All content is Markdown in Git.
  • A standalone OpenAPI specification (specs/insight-openapi.yaml) describes request parameters and validation models.
  • MkDocs Material builds the site, and GitHub Actions publishes it to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: 5. Outcomes
docs.text:
The following are design outcomes:

  • Lower cognitive load for operators. The workflow is presented as four visual steps with no code or command-line syntax.
  • Faster developer onboarding. Copyable cURL commands let an engineer start the container and run a test prediction against /predict.
  • Maintainable docs. Changes go through pull requests, the same as application code.

docs.title: InSight developer and API reference guide
docs.text: This guide provides technical specifications for integrating with and extending the InSight clinical decision support microservice. It covers environment configuration, request contracts, database side effects, and response schemas for the FastAPI inference backend.

docs.title: Service overview and runtime
docs.text:
• Framework: FastAPI (Python 3.9 or later)
  • ASGI server: Uvicorn
  • Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:8000
  • Interactive documentation (Swagger UI): http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
  • Alternative schema (ReDoc): http://127.0.0.1:8000/redoc

docs.title: Authentication and authorization
docs.text:
Clinical terminals and operators pass an authorized user_id, a universally unique identifier (UUID) that represents the authenticated doctor or nurse from Supabase Auth, in the multipart form payload:

  • Field: user_id (string / UUID)
  • Access scopes: Validated against existing Supabase authentication users, to associate patient intakes and prediction logs with specific clinical operators.

docs.title: Cataract screening and intake pipeline
docs.text:
This endpoint processes an ocular fundus scan through the ResNet-18 inference engine, generates a Grad-CAM saliency map, uploads assets to Supabase Storage, and commits audit records to PostgreSQL.

  • Path: POST /predict/
  • Endpoint URL: http://127.0.0.1:8000/predict/
  • Content-Type: multipart/form-data

docs.title: Request parameters
docs.text:
All parameters are required form-data fields:

Field Type Encoding Required Description file Binary File (UploadFile) Yes Retinal fundus image (.jpg, .jpeg, .png). patient_name string Form (str) Yes Full name or clinical pseudonym of the patient. age integer Form (int) Yes Patient age, in years. gender string Form (str) Yes Biological sex or gender identifier, for example, Female, Male, or Other. medical_history string Form (str) Yes Relevant pre-existing conditions, for example, Type 2 Diabetes, Hypertension, or None. symptoms string Form (str) Yes Self-reported visual disturbances, for example, Cloudy vision or Haloes around lights. user_id string Form (str) Yes UUID or account identifier of the screening clinician.

docs.title: Request examples
docs.text:
cURL 
    curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8000/predict/" \
      -F "file=@scans/patient_scan_01.png" \
      -F "patient_name=PAT-2026-0841" \
      -F "age=64" \
      -F "gender=Female" \
      -F "medical_history=Type 2 Diabetes" \
      -F "symptoms=Blurry vision in left eye" \
      -F "user_id=usr_9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d"
Python (Requests) 
    import requests

    api_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/predict/"

    # Prepare the multipart payload.
    payload = {
        "patient_name": "PAT-2026-0841",
        "age": 64,
        "gender": "Female",
        "medical_history": "Type 2 Diabetes",
        "symptoms": "Blurry vision in left eye",
        "user_id": "usr_9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d",
    }

    with open("scans/patient_scan_01.png", "rb") as image_file:
        files = {"file": ("patient_scan_01.png", image_file, "image/png")}
        response = requests.post(api_url, data=payload, files=files)

    print(response.status_code)
    print(response.json())

docs.title: 200 OK: inference and persistence successful
docs.text:
Returned when the scan is classified, the Grad-CAM map is generated, and the patient and prediction records are persisted to Supabase.

{
  "class": "Cataract",
  "confidence": 0.9854,
  "all_probabilities": {
    "No Cataract": 0.0146,
    "Cataract": 0.9854
  },
  "patient_id": "841b8a53-487e-4009-8ff4-938814529db7",
  "image_url": "https://your-project.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/scans/patient_scan_01.png",
  "gradcam_url": "https://your-project.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/scans/gradcam_4f09d82e-68be-4091-8d26-a07727e4eef6.png"
}

docs.title: Response field reference
docs.text: Key Type Description class string Final categorical classification: "Cataract" or "No Cataract". confidence float Softmax probability assigned to the predicted class (0.0 to 1.0). all_probabilities object Complete probability distribution across both diagnostic classes. patient_id string / int Generated primary key record ID from the patients table in Supabase. image_url string Public or pre-signed URL of the raw uploaded fundus photograph in cloud storage. gradcam_url string Public or pre-signed URL of the generated Grad-CAM saliency visualization in cloud storage.

docs.title: 422 Unprocessable Entity: missing or invalid payload
docs.text:
FastAPI returns this automatically if required form fields are missing, or if field data types don't match, for example, if you pass a string for age.

{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": ["body", "age"],
      "msg": "value is not a valid integer",
      "type": "type_error.integer"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 500 Internal Server Error: pipeline exception
docs.text:
Returned if an unhandled exception occurs during tensor transformation, the model forward pass, or the Supabase storage upload.

{
  "detail": "Failed to upload image to Supabase: Bucket not found or connection timed out."
}

Retry guidance

A 500 response indicates a server-side or infrastructure failure, not a client payload error. Retrying an identical request doesn't succeed if the underlying issue, such as a storage bucket misconfiguration, persists. Escalate to IT support if repeated 500 responses occur.

docs.title: Database side effects
docs.text:
Every successful call to POST /predict/ performs two database transactions:

  1. patients table insert: Records patient demographics, history, symptoms, the raw image URL, and the created_by clinician ID.
  2. predictions table insert: Links the new patient_id to the classification result, the confidence score, the Grad-CAM asset URL, and the clinician audit trail.

docs.title: InSight: automated cataract screening system
docs.text: InSight is an open-source clinical decision support system (CDSS) that detects cataracts in ocular fundus (retinal) images. It uses a ResNet-18 convolutional neural network (CNN) for binary classification and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) saliency maps to explain each result.

docs.title: The clinical challenge and solution
docs.text:
Cataracts are the leading cause of preventable blindness worldwide, and they disproportionately affect regions with a shortage of trained ophthalmologists.

Challenge How InSight addresses it Delayed diagnosis Automated screening lets nurses and general practitioners triage patients at the point of care. Limited trust in opaque AI Each prediction includes a Grad-CAM overlay that highlights the image regions that influenced the result. Non-medical input errors A MobileNetV2 gatekeeper model rejects non-retinal uploads before inference. Workflow disconnect The system provides an end-to-end screening workflow with automated PDF reports and audit logging.

docs.title: System architecture
docs.text:
InSight runs as a microservice and uses a service-oriented architecture to separate machine learning inference from the clinical interface:

  • Presentation layer: A Streamlit dashboard for clinicians. It supports single and batch uploads, patient lookup, and analytics.
  • Application layer: An asynchronous FastAPI backend that runs the MobileNetV2 gatekeeper, the PyTorch ResNet-18 model, and Grad-CAM computation.
  • Data and authentication layer: Supabase-managed PostgreSQL storage with role-based access control (RBAC) that separates nurse and physician roles.

docs.title: Quickstart and local setup
docs.text: To run the inference backend and the clinician dashboard locally, follow these steps.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.9 or later
  • Git

docs.title: Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/nyambura-pov/InSight_Cataract_Detection.git
cd InSight_Cataract_Detection

docs.title: Create a virtual environment and install dependencies
docs.text:
Linux / macOS 
    python3 -m venv .venv
    source .venv/bin/activate
    pip install -r requirements.txt
Windows (PowerShell) 
    python -m venv .venv
    .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
    pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Configure credentials
docs.text:
Create a .streamlit/secrets.toml file in the project root and add your Supabase credentials:

[supabase]
url = "https://PROJECT_ID.supabase.co"
key = "SUPABASE_ANON_KEY"

Replace the following:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Supabase project.
  • SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: The anonymous (anon) public key of your Supabase project.

docs.title: Start the services
docs.text:
Start the FastAPI inference server:

uvicorn backend_app:app --reload --port 8000

In a second terminal, start the clinician dashboard:

streamlit run app.py

In a browser, go to http://localhost:8501.

docs.title: Model performance
docs.text:
The ResNet-18 model was trained on the Ocular Disease Intelligent Recognition (ODIR-5K) dataset. To address class imbalance, training used focal loss (γ = 2.0). The following table shows results on a held-out test split of 1,098 fundus images.

Metric Score What it measures Recall (sensitivity) 99.40% The proportion of cataract cases that the model correctly flags. A higher value means fewer missed cases. Precision 99.00% The proportion of flagged cases that are true cataracts. Accuracy 99.52% The proportion of all predictions that are correct. F1 score 0.992 The harmonic mean of precision and recall. AUC-ROC 0.998 How well the model separates cataract from non-cataract images across all decision thresholds.

Scope of these results

These results come from one held-out split of a single public dataset. They don't measure performance on images from other cameras, populations, or clinical settings.

docs.title: License and clinical use
docs.text:
InSight is distributed under the MIT License.

Clinical use disclaimer

InSight is a clinical decision support system (CDSS) for frontline triage. It assists healthcare providers and doesn't replace diagnosis by a licensed ophthalmologist.

docs.title: Clinical operator guide: InSight cataract screening
docs.text:
Welcome to the InSight clinical decision support system (CDSS). This guide provides step-by-step instructions for clinical operators, triage nurses, and healthcare assistants to perform rapid cataract screenings, review AI-generated visual evidence, and generate patient referral documentation.

Audience: Clinical operators, triage nurses, and healthcare assistants.

Important clinical disclaimer

InSight is an automated decision support tool designed to assist in triage prioritization in resource-constrained environments. It does not provide a definitive medical diagnosis and should never replace evaluation by a licensed ophthalmologist or eye care specialist.

docs.title: Sign in to the system
docs.text:
Before you screen any patients, confirm that you have valid clinical credentials and that you know your assigned role, since available features depend on it.

  1. Open your web browser and go to the clinical portal URL (for example, https://insight-screening.internal or http://localhost:8501).
  2. On the welcome screen, enter your clinical credentials (email and password).
  3. Select Log In.
    • Note: Your user role (Nurse or Doctor) determines which features are available. If you need access to the analytics dashboard, contact your system administrator.

docs.title: Prepare retinal fundus scans
docs.text:
To ensure accurate screening and prevent processing errors, fundus photographs must meet the following intake standards:

  • Supported formats: .jpg, .jpeg, or .png.
  • Image quality: The pupil is centered, and the lens is free of external glare or eyelid obstruction.
  • Validation check (the gatekeeper): The system automatically checks incoming files. If you upload a non-retinal image, such as a facial photo, a document, or an object, the system rejects the file and shows an Invalid Image Type notification.

docs.title: Screen a single patient
docs.text:
After a scan meets the intake standards, screen it using the following workflow.

  1. In the left sidebar, go to Patient Screening > Single Scan.
  2. In the Patient Identifier field, enter the assigned patient ID (for example, PAT-2026-0841). Don't enter personal details such as names or national identity numbers.
  3. Select Browse Files, or drag and drop the file, to upload the retinal fundus image.

Figure 1: The InSight diagnostic interface ready for single or batch fundus image acquisition.

  1. Select Run Screening Analysis.
  2. After processing completes (typically 3–5 seconds), review the screening card:
    • Classification: Shows either Normal (no significant cataract indications) or Cataract Detected.
    • Confidence level: Shows a percentage that indicates the model's certainty.

docs.title: Read the Grad-CAM heatmap
docs.text:
When InSight classifies an image, it provides an explainable visual overlay called a Grad-CAM saliency map. This map helps you verify why the model flagged a scan.

Figure 2: Screening result displaying positive cataract detection (92.5% confidence) alongside the Grad-CAM saliency overlay and urgent referral notice.

Heatmap color Clinical meaning Recommended action 🔴 Deep red / orange Area of highest visual importance to the AI, typically localized lens opacity or clouding. Visually inspect this exact anatomical region for cataract signs. 🟡 Yellow / green Moderate influence on the screening decision. Treat as a secondary area of interest. 🔵 Blue / violet Minimal to no influence; normal ocular structures. No action needed; no abnormalities are flagged here.

Clinical tip

If the model flags Cataract Detected, but the red heatmap highlights an eyelash, an eyelid shadow, or a camera artifact rather than the lens or pupil, treat the result as inconclusive and recapture the scan.

docs.title: Export a referral report as PDF
docs.text:
If a patient requires referral or physical documentation, operators can generate and download audit records directly from the results view:

  1. Review the generated Grad-CAM overlay and confirmation prompts.
  2. Select Export PDF Report to compile the clinical summary, or select Export Grad-CAM to download the standalone visual asset.

Figure 3: Action controls for saving results, exporting the referral PDF, and extracting Grad-CAM visual assets.

The generated single-page PDF report formats patient metadata, quantitative confidence scores, diagnostic recommendations, and side-by-side retinal visualizations for specialist review.

Figure 4: Sample InSight clinical referral document generated for specialist handoff.

docs.title: Reviewing patient screening history
docs.text:
Operators can retrieve prior screening records and historical reports using the patient tracking module:

  1. In the left navigation menu, select Patient History.
  2. Enter the assigned Patient Identifier (for example, PATIENT-024) and select Search History.
  3. Review the historical record table for previous screening timestamps, classification outcomes, confidence scores, and operator IDs.

Figure 5: Historical screening log displaying prior intake records and diagnostic results.

docs.title: Troubleshoot common intake issues
docs.text: Problem Probable cause Corrective action Invalid Image Type error banner The image failed the pre-validation gatekeeper check, for example, a blurry scan or a non-fundus picture. Confirm that the file is a clean fundus scan of the eye, not an external camera photo. File Size Exceeded alert The scan resolution exceeds the maximum upload limit, typically 10 MB. Compress or resize the image before you upload it. Processing spinner freezes A temporary network interruption occurred between the terminal and the backend service. Refresh your browser window and retry the upload. If the issue persists, contact IT support.

docs.title: Send your first email with the Resend API
docs.text:
Independent sample

This is an independent documentation sample written for a technical writing portfolio. It is not official Resend documentation.

Time to complete: about 5 minutes

In this quickstart, you will:

  • Set your API key as an environment variable.
  • Send a test email with cURL or Python.
  • Capture the email id from the response.
  • Check the delivery status of your email.

Resend exposes a REST API over HTTPS. Requests and responses use JSON, and every request is authenticated with a Bearer token.

Property Value Base URL https://api.resend.com Authentication Authorization: Bearer <API key> Content type application/json Default rate limit 2 requests per second per team

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
You need:

  1. A Resend account.
  2. An API key. In the Resend dashboard, go to API Keys and create a key with Full access. Keys start with re_. Copy the key right away, because Resend shows it only once.
  3. A sender address. To test without a custom domain, use onboarding@resend.dev.
  4. For the Python examples, Python 3 and the requests library (pip install requests).

docs.title: Set your API key
docs.text:
Store your key in an environment variable so it never ends up in source control. Run the command in the same terminal window you will use for the next steps. The variable lasts only for that window, so set it again if you open a new one.

Linux / macOS 
    export RESEND_API_KEY="re_your_api_key"
Windows (PowerShell) 
    $env:RESEND_API_KEY="re_your_api_key"

docs.title: Step 1: Send an email
docs.text:
The recipient delivered@resend.dev is a Resend test address that simulates a successful delivery, so you don't need a real inbox.

cURL (Linux / macOS) 
    curl -X POST https://api.resend.com/emails \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
        "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
        "subject": "Hello from the Resend API",
        "html": "<p>Congrats on sending your first email with <strong>Resend</strong>!</p>"
      }'
Python

Save this as send_email.py, then run python send_email.py.

    import os
    import requests

    api_key = os.environ.get("RESEND_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise SystemExit("Set the RESEND_API_KEY environment variable first.")

    response = requests.post(
        "https://api.resend.com/emails",
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        json={
            "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
            "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
            "subject": "Hello from the Resend API",
            "html": "<p>Congrats on sending your first email with <strong>Resend</strong>!</p>",
        },
    )
    print(response.status_code)
    print(response.json())

Using Windows PowerShell?

PowerShell's curl is an alias for a different command. Use the Python example, or run curl.exe with backtick (`) line continuations.

docs.title: Step 2: Confirm the response
docs.text:
A successful request returns 200 OK and the ID of your email:

{
  "id": "01a13c69-fa51-7d25-9158-ef0e1ac508a7"
}

Save the email ID

You need the id to check delivery status in the next step.

A 200 response means Resend accepted the email for delivery. It doesn't mean the email has arrived yet. The next step checks that.

docs.title: Step 3: Check delivery status
docs.text:
Send a GET request to /emails/{id}. Replace the ID below with yours.

cURL 
    curl https://api.resend.com/emails/01a13c69-fa51-7d25-9158-ef0e1ac508a7 \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY"
Python

Save this as get_email.py, then run python get_email.py YOUR_EMAIL_ID.

    import os
    import sys
    import requests

    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        raise SystemExit("Usage: python get_email.py <email_id>")

    response = requests.get(
        f"https://api.resend.com/emails/{sys.argv[1]}",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['RESEND_API_KEY']}"},
    )
    print(response.status_code)
    print(response.json())

Example response:

{
  "object": "email",
  "id": "01a13c69-fa51-7d25-9158-ef0e1ac508a7",
  "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
  "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
  "created_at": "2026-10-14 21:55:40.924000+00",
  "subject": "Hello from the Resend API",
  "bcc": null,
  "cc": null,
  "reply_to": null,
  "last_event": "delivered",
  "scheduled_at": null,
  "message_id": "<010001a13c69fbd4-f6c90015-97e9-4569-93cf-c5b787ae658f-000000@email.amazonses.com>",
  "html": "<p>Congrats on sending your first email with <strong>Resend</strong>!</p>",
  "text": "Congrats on sending your first email with Resend!"
}

last_event shows the most recent delivery event. For test addresses like delivered@resend.dev, it can read delivered almost immediately. For other recipients, it may read sent first. Run the request again after a few seconds to see the update.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Status Likely cause Fix 401 Missing or invalid API key Check that RESEND_API_KEY is set in this terminal window and copied in full. 403 The from domain isn't verified Use onboarding@resend.dev, or verify your domain in the dashboard. 404 No email with that ID Check that the id is copied correctly. 422 A required field is missing Read message, which names the missing field. 429 Rate limit exceeded Limit requests to 2 per second, then retry.

For the full list, see Error codes.

docs.title: Case study: developer onboarding and diagnostics for the Resend API
docs.text: How I structured a quickstart, reference, and troubleshooting set for a transactional email API, and verified it against the live service.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Project Resend API documentation sample Role Technical writer and documentation engineer Deliverables Quickstart, API reference, batch guide, error catalog, troubleshooting guide, OpenAPI specification Tools and standards OpenAPI 3.1, MkDocs Material, Python (requests), cURL, Git Goals Under 5 minutes to a first successful call, no credentials in code, readers can resolve common failures themselves

This is an independent sample, not official Resend documentation.

docs.title: 1. The problem
docs.text:
Email APIs have predictable failure points for new developers:

  • Slow onboarding. Long setup and unclear prerequisites delay the first successful request.
  • Schema guesswork. If the docs don't say whether to takes a string or an array, readers hit 422 errors.
  • Silent failures. Missing DNS records, rate limits, and webhook signature mismatches fail in ways that are hard to trace.

The goal was a documentation set and OpenAPI specification that lets a developer authenticate, send an email, check its delivery status, and fix common failures without help.

docs.title: 2. Information architecture
docs.text:
Developers use API docs in three situations: getting started, looking something up, and fixing a problem. I gave each its own track:

Resend documentation
├── Get started (index.md)
│   └── Prerequisites → API key → first send → check status
├── Look up (reference.md, batch-emails.md)
│   └── Endpoints → parameter tables → payloads → batch limits
├── Fix problems (errors.md, troubleshooting.md)
│   └── Error catalog → triage table → DNS and webhook fixes
└── Machine-readable contract (specs/resend-openapi.yaml)
    └── OpenAPI specification

docs.title: 3. Key decisions
docs.text:
A. Faster first call with test addresses. Developers often give up when they must verify a domain before testing. The quickstart uses Resend's test sender onboarding@resend.dev and test recipient delivered@resend.dev, so no DNS changes are needed.

B. Credentials stay out of code. Every snippet reads RESEND_API_KEY from an environment variable. The quickstart shows the Linux/macOS and PowerShell commands, and warns that PowerShell's curl is an alias for a different command.

C. Accepted does not mean delivered. A 200 OK from POST /emails means the email was queued, not delivered. The docs explain the two steps:

POST /emails        →  200 OK with an id  (accepted)
GET /emails/{id}    →  last_event: sent → delivered  (outcome)

D. Diagnostics with runnable commands. The troubleshooting guide pairs each explanation with a command or code sample, such as dig and Resolve-DnsName for DNS records, and raw-body handlers for webhook signatures.

docs.title: 4. Verification
docs.text:
I ran the documented requests against the live API and corrected my drafts to match.

Tested: POST /emails, POST /emails/batch, GET /emails/{id}, and the 401, 403, 404, and 422 errors. Testing ran on Windows PowerShell using Python.

What testing changed:

  • Empty cc, bcc, and reply_to fields return null, not [].
  • created_at is not ISO 8601 (2026-10-14 21:55:40.924000+00).
  • The plain-text body is generated automatically when only html is sent.
  • A missing field, an invalid key, and an unverified domain all return name: "validation_error", so the error catalog tells readers to check statusCode and message too.

Not yet tested: rate-limit (429) behavior, webhooks, DNS verification, the Idempotency-Key header, and the cURL commands on Linux or macOS. Those sections follow vendor documentation.

docs.title: 5. Outcomes
docs.text:
The following are design outcomes:

  • A reader can configure a key, send an email, and check its status in one sitting without a custom domain.
  • The reference tables state types and allowed values, so readers don't have to guess at request formats.
  • The OpenAPI specification can be used to generate SDKs, run contract tests, and render interactive docs.

docs.title: Send batch emails
docs.text:
Independent sample

This is an independent documentation sample written for a technical writing portfolio. It is not official Resend documentation.

Use the batch endpoint to send up to 100 emails in a single API call. Batching reduces network overhead and helps you stay within the rate limit of 2 requests per second.

Time to complete: about 5 minutes

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text: Complete Send your first email first. You need an API key stored in the RESEND_API_KEY environment variable in your current terminal window.

docs.title: How it differs from a single send
docs.text:
POST /emails POST /emails/batch Request body One email object An array of email objects Maximum 1 email 100 emails Response { "id": "..." } { "data": [{ "id": "..." }, ...] }

Batch limitations

  • Maximum of 100 emails per request.
  • Attachments and scheduled sending are not supported in batch requests.

docs.title: Step 1: Send a batch
docs.text:
cURL (Linux / macOS) 
    curl -X POST https://api.resend.com/emails/batch \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '[
        {
          "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
          "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
          "subject": "Your order has shipped",
          "html": "<p>Your order is on its way.</p>"
        },
        {
          "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
          "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
          "subject": "Welcome to Acme",
          "html": "<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>"
        }
      ]'
Python

Save this as send_batch.py, then run python send_batch.py.

    import os
    import requests

    api_key = os.environ.get("RESEND_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise SystemExit("Set the RESEND_API_KEY environment variable first.")

    emails = [
        {
            "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
            "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
            "subject": "Your order has shipped",
            "html": "<p>Your order is on its way.</p>",
        },
        {
            "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
            "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
            "subject": "Welcome to Acme",
            "html": "<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>",
        },
    ]

    response = requests.post(
        "https://api.resend.com/emails/batch",
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        json=emails,
    )
    print(response.status_code)
    print(response.json())

Using Windows PowerShell?

Use the Python example, or run curl.exe with backtick (`) line continuations.

docs.title: Step 2: Read the response
docs.text:
A successful request returns 200 OK with one id per email, in the same order as your request:

{
  "data": [
    { "id": "01a13c71-c142-788f-ab5c-011036e2c098" },
    { "id": "01a13c71-c142-7775-a562-3f5143e032db" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Step 3: Check an email's status
docs.text:
Use any id from the response with GET /emails/{id}:

curl https://api.resend.com/emails/01a13c71-c142-7775-a562-3f5143e032db \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY"

The response shows the second email from the batch:

{
  "object": "email",
  "id": "01a13c71-c142-7775-a562-3f5143e032db",
  "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
  "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
  "created_at": "2026-10-14 22:04:10.646000+00",
  "subject": "Welcome to Acme",
  "bcc": null,
  "cc": null,
  "reply_to": null,
  "last_event": "delivered",
  "scheduled_at": null,
  "message_id": "<010001a13c71c29a-956086db-4c51-46dc-a14a-0aa5292aba73-000000@email.amazonses.com>",
  "html": "<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>",
  "text": "Thanks for signing up."
}

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Status Likely cause Fix 401 Missing or invalid API key Check that RESEND_API_KEY is set in this terminal window and copied in full. 403 A from domain isn't verified Use onboarding@resend.dev, or verify your domain in the dashboard. 422 An email in the array has a missing or invalid field Read message, which names the problem. Check every object in the array. 429 Rate limit exceeded Limit requests to 2 per second, then retry.

For the full list, see Error codes.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
Independent sample

This is an independent documentation sample written for a technical writing portfolio. It is not official Resend documentation.

When a request fails, the Resend API returns a non-2xx HTTP status code and a JSON body that describes the problem. Use this page to identify the cause and decide whether to fix the request or retry it.

docs.title: Error response format
docs.text:
{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "name": "validation_error",
  "message": "Missing `subject` field."
}
Field Type Description statusCode integer The HTTP status code of the response. name string The error category. Different problems can share the same name, so also check statusCode and message. message string A human-readable explanation of what went wrong.

Check more than the error name

A missing field, an invalid API key and an unverified domain all return name: "validation_error". Use statusCode to tell them apart, and read message for the specific cause.

docs.title: Error catalog
docs.text:
These errors were reproduced against the live API.

Status name Example message Cause How to fix it 401 validation_error API key is invalid The API key is invalid. Check that RESEND_API_KEY is set and copied in full. 403 validation_error The gmail.com domain is not verified. Please, add and verify your domain on https://resend.com/domains The from address uses an unverified domain. Verify your domain, or use onboarding@resend.dev. 404 not_found Email not found No email exists with that ID. Check the email id. 422 validation_error Missing `subject` field. A required field is missing. Add the field named in message.

Other errors can occur. For example, the API returns 429 when you exceed the rate limit of 2 requests per second, and 5xx when something fails on Resend's side. Neither was reproduced for this page.

docs.title: Which errors to retry
docs.text: Status Retry? Why 4xx except 429 No The request itself is wrong. Retrying sends the same bad request. 429 Yes, after a delay The request was valid but you exceeded a limit. 5xx Yes, after a delay The failure is temporary and on the server side.

docs.title: Retry safely
docs.text:
Retrying a send can deliver the same email twice if the first attempt actually succeeded. Send the same Idempotency-Key header on every attempt so Resend treats the retries as one request. Increase the wait between attempts (exponential backoff).

import os
import time
import uuid

import requests

URL = "https://api.resend.com/emails"


def send_with_retry(payload, max_attempts=5):
    api_key = os.environ["RESEND_API_KEY"]
    idempotency_key = str(uuid.uuid4())  # same key for every attempt

    for attempt in range(max_attempts):
        response = requests.post(
            URL,
            headers={
                "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
                "Idempotency-Key": idempotency_key,
            },
            json=payload,
            timeout=10,
        )

        if response.status_code == 429 or response.status_code >= 500:
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)  # wait 1, 2, 4, 8 seconds
            continue

        response.raise_for_status()  # raises for non-retryable 4xx errors
        return response.json()

    raise RuntimeError(f"Email not sent after {max_attempts} attempts.")

docs.title: Test error handling
docs.text:
Trigger an error on purpose to confirm your handling works:

To trigger Do this Result Missing field Omit the subject field. 422 Invalid key Set RESEND_API_KEY to a key that doesn't exist. 401 Unverified sender Set from to an address at a domain you haven't verified. 403 Unknown email Request GET /emails/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000. 404

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Independent sample

This is an independent documentation sample written for a technical writing portfolio. It is not official Resend documentation.

This page describes the Resend API endpoints covered in this documentation set. For a guided introduction, see Send your first email.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Property Value Base URL https://api.resend.com Authentication Authorization: Bearer <API key> Content type application/json Default rate limit 2 requests per second per team

All requests must use HTTPS. For the machine-readable contract, see the OpenAPI specification or download the YAML.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description POST /emails Send a single email. POST /emails/batch Send up to 100 emails in one request. GET /emails/{id} Retrieve an email and its latest delivery status.

docs.title: Send an email
docs.text:
Sends a single email to one or more recipients.

POST /emails

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Required Description Authorization Yes Bearer <API key> Content-Type Yes Must be application/json. Idempotency-Key No A unique string that prevents duplicate sends when you retry a request.

docs.title: Request body
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description from string Yes Sender address, for example Acme <billing@acme.com>. Must use a verified domain, or onboarding@resend.dev for testing. to string or array Yes One recipient address, or an array of up to 50 addresses. subject string Yes The email subject line. html string Conditional The HTML body. Provide html, text, or both. text string Conditional The plain-text body. If you send only html, Resend generates a plain-text version. cc string or array No Carbon copy recipient addresses. bcc string or array No Blind carbon copy recipient addresses. reply_to string or array No Address or addresses that replies are sent to. headers object No Custom key-value pairs added to the email headers.

docs.title: Example request
docs.text:
cURL 
    curl -X POST https://api.resend.com/emails \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
        "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
        "subject": "Hello from the Resend API",
        "html": "<p>Congrats on sending your first email with <strong>Resend</strong>!</p>"
      }'
Python 
    import os
    import requests

    response = requests.post(
        "https://api.resend.com/emails",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['RESEND_API_KEY']}"},
        json={
            "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
            "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
            "subject": "Hello from the Resend API",
            "html": "<p>Congrats on sending your first email with <strong>Resend</strong>!</p>",
        },
    )
    print(response.status_code, response.json())

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
A successful request returns 200 OK:

{
  "id": "01a13c69-fa51-7d25-9158-ef0e1ac508a7"
}
Property Type Description id string The unique identifier of the email. Use it to retrieve the email.

A 200 response means Resend accepted the email for delivery. It does not mean the email has been delivered yet.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Cause 401 The API key is invalid. 403 The from address uses an unverified domain. 422 A required field, such as subject, is missing.

See Error codes for example messages.

docs.title: Send batch emails
docs.text:
Sends up to 100 emails in a single request.

POST /emails/batch

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Same as Send an email.

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
An array of 1 to 100 email objects. Each object accepts the same parameters as Send an email.

Batch limitations

  • Maximum of 100 emails per request.
  • Attachments and scheduled sending are not supported in batch requests.

docs.title: Example request
docs.text:
cURL 
    curl -X POST https://api.resend.com/emails/batch \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '[
        {
          "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
          "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
          "subject": "Your order has shipped",
          "html": "<p>Your order is on its way.</p>"
        },
        {
          "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
          "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
          "subject": "Welcome to Acme",
          "html": "<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>"
        }
      ]'

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
A successful request returns 200 OK with one id per email, in the same order as the request:

{
  "data": [
    { "id": "01a13c71-c142-788f-ab5c-011036e2c098" },
    { "id": "01a13c71-c142-7775-a562-3f5143e032db" }
  ]
}
Property Type Description data array One object per email, in request order. data[].id string The unique identifier of that email.

For a task-based walkthrough, see Send batch emails.

docs.title: Retrieve an email
docs.text:
Returns the details and latest delivery status of an email you sent.

GET /emails/{id}

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Required Description Authorization Yes Bearer <API key>

docs.title: Path parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes The id returned when the email was sent.

docs.title: Example request
docs.text:
cURL 
    curl https://api.resend.com/emails/01a13c69-fa51-7d25-9158-ef0e1ac508a7 \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY"
Python 
    import os
    import requests

    email_id = "01a13c69-fa51-7d25-9158-ef0e1ac508a7"
    response = requests.get(
        f"https://api.resend.com/emails/{email_id}",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['RESEND_API_KEY']}"},
    )
    print(response.json())

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
A successful request returns 200 OK:

{
  "object": "email",
  "id": "01a13c69-fa51-7d25-9158-ef0e1ac508a7",
  "to": ["delivered@resend.dev"],
  "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
  "created_at": "2026-10-14 21:55:40.924000+00",
  "subject": "Hello from the Resend API",
  "bcc": null,
  "cc": null,
  "reply_to": null,
  "last_event": "delivered",
  "scheduled_at": null,
  "message_id": "<010001a13c69fbd4-f6c90015-97e9-4569-93cf-c5b787ae658f-000000@email.amazonses.com>",
  "html": "<p>Congrats on sending your first email with <strong>Resend</strong>!</p>",
  "text": "Congrats on sending your first email with Resend!"
}
Property Type Description object string The object type. Always email. id string The unique identifier of the email. from string The sender address. to array The recipient addresses. subject string The subject line. html string or null The HTML body, if one was sent. text string or null The plain-text body. If you send only html, Resend generates this from it. cc, bcc, reply_to array or null The addresses supplied for each field. null if none were set. created_at string When the email was created, for example 2026-10-14 21:55:40.924000+00. scheduled_at string or null When the email is scheduled to send. null if it isn't scheduled. message_id string The message ID assigned to the email. last_event string The most recent delivery event. Values include sent, delivered, delivery_delayed, bounced, complained and opened.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Cause 401 The API key is invalid. 404 No email exists with that ID.

See Error codes for example messages.

docs.title: Case study: writing a symptom-first troubleshooting guide
docs.text: How I designed a troubleshooting guide that helps a developer find and fix a failure quickly.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Project Troubleshooting guide for the Resend API Artifact docs/resend/troubleshooting.md (the InSight runbook is in docs/troubleshooting-runbooks.md) Role Technical writer and documentation engineer Contents Triage table, error runbooks, DNS checks, webhook handlers, support checklist, glossary Tools Markdown, MkDocs Material, dig, PowerShell Resolve-DnsName, Node.js (Express), Python (FastAPI) Goals Find the right section within seconds, fix without contacting support, calm and neutral tone

docs.title: 1. The problem
docs.text:
When something fails in production, the reader is stressed and wants a fix, not a lecture. Troubleshooting docs often fail them in three ways:

  • Organized by cause, not symptom. The reader sees 403 Domain is not verified but must already know the root cause to find the right page.
  • Filler and condescension. Words like "simply," "just," and "obviously" add frustration without adding information.
  • Advice without commands. "Verify your keys" doesn't help without a command to run or code to copy.

docs.title: 2. Structure
docs.text:
Each problem follows the same path:

1. Triage table      Match the error code or symptom to a section
2. Cause             State why it happens
3. Fix               Platform-specific commands and code
4. Escalation        What to collect before contacting support

docs.title: 3. Key decisions
docs.text:
A. Triage table first. The table sits at the top, before any narrative. It maps each symptom (401, 403, 404, 422, 429, silent webhooks) to a likely cause, a first check, and a link to its section.

B. Neutral, blame-free tone. Instructions describe what the system does, not what the reader did wrong.

  • Before: "You are calculating the signature wrong because you parsed the body."
  • After: "Signature verification fails when the body your code checks differs from the body Resend sent."

Terms are defined once, in a sentence, where they first appear. There are no analogies or "in plain terms" boxes, because the readers are technical and mid-problem.

C. Commands for both platforms. DNS and environment checks show Linux/macOS and PowerShell side by side (dig and Resolve-DnsName), so a Windows engineer isn't told to run a Unix tool.

D. The raw-body webhook problem. Web frameworks parse JSON by default, which can change spacing or key order and break the HMAC signature. The guide shows how to read the unmodified body in Express (express.raw()) and FastAPI (await request.body()) and use a verification library.

docs.title: 4. Escalation
docs.text:
The guide ends with "When to contact support," which lists what to collect first:

  • The email id.
  • The time of the request, with time zone.
  • The statusCode, name, and message.
  • The request, with the API key removed.

It also warns never to share API keys (re_...) or webhook signing secrets (whsec_...).

docs.title: 5. Verification
docs.text:
Tested against the live API: the 401, 403, 404, and 422 error messages shown in the guide are real output.

Based on vendor documentation, not yet tested: DNS verification, webhooks, and rate limits. The code samples follow Resend's and Svix's documented behavior but haven't been run.

docs.title: 6. Outcomes
docs.text:
The following are design outcomes:

  • A reader can match a symptom to a fix without reading the whole page.
  • Every fix includes something to run or copy.
  • The support checklist helps readers file a report that support can act on.

docs.title: Troubleshooting guide
docs.text:
Independent sample

This is an independent documentation sample written for a technical writing portfolio. It is not official Resend documentation.

This guide helps you diagnose and fix common problems when sending email with the Resend API: failed requests, domain verification errors, webhook problems, and rate limits.

Find your symptom in the table below, then follow the link to the matching section. Each section lists the symptom, the likely cause, and the fix.

docs.title: Quick triage
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause First check Go to 401 when sending or retrieving The API key is invalid or not set Confirm RESEND_API_KEY is set in this terminal window Invalid API key 403 when sending The from domain isn't verified Check the domain status in the dashboard Domain not verified 404 when retrieving an email The email ID is wrong Compare the ID with the one the send request returned Email not found 422 when sending A required field is missing Read message, which names the field Missing field 429 on bursts of requests The request rate exceeds 2 per second Count your requests per second Rate limits Your webhook receives nothing Your endpoint is unreachable or returns errors Check the delivery log in the Resend dashboard No webhook events Your app rejects a webhook as invalid The signature check failed Confirm you verify the raw request body Signature verification

docs.title: Read the error first
docs.text:
Every failed API request returns a JSON error with three fields:

{
  "statusCode": 403,
  "name": "validation_error",
  "message": "The gmail.com domain is not verified. Please, add and verify your domain on https://resend.com/domains"
}

Different problems can share the same name. In testing, a missing field, an invalid API key, and an unverified domain all returned validation_error. Use statusCode to narrow down the problem, and read message for the exact cause.

docs.title: API request errors
docs.text: The errors in this section were reproduced against the live API.

docs.title: 401: API key is invalid
docs.text:
Symptom

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "name": "validation_error",
  "message": "API key is invalid"
}

Cause: The key is wrong, was deleted, was copied incompletely, or isn't set in the terminal window you're running the command from.

Fix

Step 1. Check that the variable is set in the current window:

Linux / macOS 
    [ -n "$RESEND_API_KEY" ] && echo "Key is set" || echo "Key is NOT set"
Windows (PowerShell) 
    if ($env:RESEND_API_KEY) { "Key is set" } else { "Key is NOT set" }

Step 2. If the key isn't set, set it again. An environment variable set in one terminal window isn't available in another.

Step 3. If the key is set, create a new key in the dashboard under API Keys and replace the old one. Don't commit API keys to Git.

docs.title: 403: Domain is not verified
docs.text:
Symptom

{
  "statusCode": 403,
  "name": "validation_error",
  "message": "The gmail.com domain is not verified. Please, add and verify your domain on https://resend.com/domains"
}

Cause: The from address uses a domain that hasn't been verified for your account. You can't send from domains you don't control, such as gmail.com.

Fix

  • To test: use onboarding@resend.dev as the from address.
  • To send from your own domain: verify it. See Domain authentication.

docs.title: 404: Email not found
docs.text:
Symptom

{
  "statusCode": 404,
  "name": "not_found",
  "message": "Email not found"
}

Cause: No email exists with that ID.

Fix: Compare the ID in your request with the id returned when you sent the email. Copy and paste the ID rather than retyping it.

docs.title: 422: Missing required field
docs.text:
Symptom

{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "name": "validation_error",
  "message": "Missing `subject` field."
}

Cause: The request body is missing a required field.

Fix: Add the field named in message. Every send requires from, to, and subject, plus an html or text body.

docs.title: Domain authentication and DNS
docs.text:
Receiving mail servers check that the sender is authorized to use the domain in the from address. Resend relies on two DNS-based checks:

  • SPF lists the servers that are allowed to send email for your domain.
  • DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to each message, which receivers verify against a public key published in your DNS.

Both are published as DNS records at your DNS provider. If the records are missing or incorrect, the domain fails verification, and sending from it returns a 403 error.

docs.title: Domain verification fails
docs.text:
Symptom: Sending returns a 403 error, or the domain shows as pending or failed in the dashboard.

Cause: The DNS records provided by Resend are missing, mistyped, or have not propagated yet. Propagation is the time it takes for a DNS change to become visible across the internet.

Diagnose

Step 1. Open the Resend dashboard, go to Domains, and open your domain. Copy the exact record names and values shown there.

Step 2. Check whether the record is live. Replace the name below with the DKIM record name from your dashboard:

Linux / macOS 
    dig TXT resend._domainkey.yourdomain.com +short
Windows (PowerShell) 
    Resolve-DnsName -Name "resend._domainkey.yourdomain.com" -Type TXT

Step 3. If the command returns nothing, the record isn't published yet or contains a typo.

Fix

  1. At your DNS provider (for example Cloudflare, Route 53, or Namecheap), create every record exactly as shown in the Resend dashboard. Some providers append your domain name automatically, so check for doubled names such as resend._domainkey.yourdomain.com.yourdomain.com.
  2. Wait for propagation. Changes can take from a few minutes to 48 hours. Lowering the record's TTL (the time DNS servers cache it) to 300 seconds before you make changes shortens the wait for later updates.
  3. Return to the dashboard and run verification again.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: A webhook is an HTTP request that Resend sends to your server when an event occurs, such as an email being delivered or bouncing. Use webhooks instead of polling GET /emails/{id} when you need to react to delivery events.

docs.title: No webhook events arrive
docs.text:
Symptom: You registered a webhook, but your server receives nothing.

Likely causes

  • Your endpoint isn't reachable from the public internet, for example because it runs only on localhost.
  • Your endpoint doesn't have a valid HTTPS certificate.
  • Your endpoint responds slowly or returns an error status.

Fix

  1. In the Resend dashboard, open Webhooks and check the delivery log for your endpoint. It shows the status code your server returned.
  2. Confirm the endpoint URL is public and uses HTTPS. When developing locally, use a tunneling tool to expose your local server temporarily.
  3. Return a 2xx status quickly. Do slow work, such as database writes, after you respond.
  4. See Resend's webhook documentation for how failed deliveries are retried.

docs.title: Signature verification fails
docs.text:
Resend signs each webhook so that you can confirm it came from Resend and was not modified. The signature is an HMAC, a code computed from the request body and a signing secret that only you and Resend know. Verification fails when the body your code checks differs from the body Resend sent.

Symptom: Your server rejects webhooks as having an invalid signature. Your application might respond with 401 or log a message such as "signature verification failed". That response comes from your code, not from Resend.

Likely causes

  • Your framework parsed the JSON body before you verified it. Re-serializing parsed JSON can change spacing or key order, which changes the signature.
  • The signing secret in your environment doesn't match the secret for this webhook endpoint. Signing secrets start with whsec_.
  • The verification step doesn't receive the signature headers.

Fix

  1. Verify the raw body. Read the request body as unmodified bytes or text, and pass that to the verifier.
  2. Use a verification library instead of writing the HMAC check yourself. Resend delivers webhooks through Svix, which provides libraries for this.
  3. Pass the three headers: svix-id, svix-timestamp, and svix-signature.
  4. Check the secret. Compare RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET with the signing secret shown for the endpoint in the dashboard.

Example handlers that verify the raw body:

Node.js (Express) 
    import express from "express";
    import { Webhook } from "svix";

    const app = express();

    // express.raw() keeps the body unparsed for this route only.
    app.post(
      "/api/webhooks",
      express.raw({ type: "application/json" }),
      (req, res) => {
        const wh = new Webhook(process.env.RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET);
        try {
          const event = wh.verify(req.body.toString(), req.headers);
          // Handle the verified event here.
          res.sendStatus(200);
        } catch (err) {
          res.sendStatus(400); // Signature check failed.
        }
      }
    );
Python (FastAPI) 
    import os

    from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
    from svix.webhooks import Webhook, WebhookVerificationError

    app = FastAPI()


    @app.post("/api/webhooks")
    async def handle_webhook(request: Request):
        raw_body = await request.body()  # unparsed bytes
        wh = Webhook(os.environ["RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET"])
        try:
            event = wh.verify(raw_body, dict(request.headers))
        except WebhookVerificationError:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid signature")
        # Handle the verified event here.
        return {"ok": True}

docs.title: Rate limits (429)
docs.text:
The default rate limit is 2 requests per second per team. Requests over the limit are rejected with 429 Too Many Requests. The request itself is valid, and it can succeed if you send it again at a lower rate.

Symptom: Bursts of requests return 429, while the same requests succeed when sent more slowly.

Cause: Your application sent more than 2 requests in one second.

Fix

  • Batch your sends. One call to POST /emails/batch can carry up to 100 emails and counts as a single request. See Send batch emails.
  • Queue and pace requests. Place outgoing emails in a background queue, such as Celery or BullMQ, and have workers send at a controlled rate.
  • Retry with backoff. When you receive a 429, wait and retry, waiting longer after each failed attempt. See Retry safely.

docs.title: When to contact support
docs.text:
If the problem remains after you've followed the steps above, collect the following before you contact support:

  • The email id returned by the API.
  • The time of the request, including the time zone.
  • The statusCode, name, and message from the error.
  • The request you sent, with the API key removed.

Don't share your API key or webhook signing secret with anyone, including support.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition API key A secret string that identifies your account in API requests. Bearer token A credential sent in the Authorization header. Resend API keys are sent this way. DKIM A cryptographic signature added to each email and verified against a public key in DNS. DNS The system that maps domain names to the records published for them. HMAC A code computed from a message and a shared secret, used to verify the sender and detect changes. Idempotency key A unique value sent with a request so that retries don't create duplicates. Propagation The time a DNS change takes to become visible across the internet. Rate limit The maximum number of requests allowed in a given period. SPF A DNS record that lists the servers allowed to send email for a domain. Webhook An HTTP request sent by a service to your server when an event occurs.
